citations.claim: outgoing speed after collision larger than incoming despite e<1
violating energy at step 7 exceeds 900.4 allowed

counterfactual.change: Set restitution e from 0.91279 to 0.0; with e=0 collision dissipates energy and passes energy_bound. This isolates that the energy gain is caused by restitution handling during thin-wall collision.

explanation: High-speed (vx~38.9) collision with ultra-thin wall (w=0.1) in substepped integration produces energy gain. Incoming speed magnitude at step6 is ~38.9, outgoing at step7 is ~41.3 despite e=0.91 which should conserve or lose energy. Speed increases from ~38.9 to ~41.34, total energy rises from 814 to 911 J exceeding E0+10% tolerance. Likely cause: collision with thin box using positional correction and impulse calculation during substeps adds energy when body grazes edge, or restitution applied to already-corrected velocity.
vision_note: In frames 4-6 the blue violating body moves fast from the left almost directly into the very top tip of the thin vertical wall, grazing the corner. At frame 7 it is still in contact at that tip and has been deflected slightly down/left, showing a high-speed corner collision with the ultra-thin wall rather than clean tunneling or exit.
